changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders and the CFOs they report to, lead with: See your own approvals by country, card type and issuer, with the reasons behind your declines. Your numbers, not an average. Say "approvals", not authorization. Move the average-uplift figure to supporting proof after the customer-specific offer.
changes.why: We pitched the Authorization Boost average and Stefan rejected it ("that's an average. What's mine?", "I can't take an average to my CFO."), while Adyen won by showing results by country, card type and issuer in his own traffic.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with a dedicated payments owner: A named person at Stripe looks at your approvals every month and tells you what to fix. Sell the named owner and the monthly review, not response-time tiers.
changes.why: Stefan asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, and Stefan said he only heard from us when he said he was leaving, even though our later analysis had fixable findings.

changes.change: For CFO-level proof in competitive renewals, add a line and a one-page asset in the buyer's language: Money left on the table, by market, in your own numbers. State the customer's own revenue at stake by country instead of a general ROI claim.
changes.why: The CFO made the decision on Stefan's recommendation, Stefan framed the problem as "Money left on the table.", and he said he could not take an average to his CFO, so the proof had to be customer-specific and framed as revenue.
